question: explain data engineering in simple words

plain3.answer: Data engineering is about moving, manipulating, and managing data [Ch. 1]. It involves developing systems that take raw data and produce high-quality information for analysis and machine learning [Ch. 1]. Data engineers ensure data is available and usable by others, setting up and operating the organization’s data infrastructure [Ch. 1]. Data engineering is the intersection of security, data management, DataOps, data architecture, orchestration, and software engineering [Ch. 1].

question: explain batch and streaming in simple words

plain3.answer: Batch processing involves handling data in large chunks at predetermined intervals or when a preset size is reached [Ch. 2]. Streaming ingestion provides data to downstream systems continuously and in real-time [Ch. 2]. Batch processing is popular in analytics and machine learning [Ch. 2]. Micro-batching is a way to use batch-oriented frameworks for streaming situations [Ch. 8]. True streaming systems process one event at a time but can still operate in batches [Ch. 8].

question: explain when an insert-only table is useful in simple words

plain3.answer: An insert-only table is useful for maintaining a current view of data [Ch. 8]. It allows new records to be inserted without deleting old ones, enabling a query to present the latest state by finding the newest record [Ch. 8]. This pattern works well for applications needing access to history, such as a banking application [Ch. 5]. However, it can be computationally expensive to find the latest record at query time [Ch. 8].
